## Bio

I am a physics PhD student at the **University of Massachusetts Amherst**, working with Prof. Benjamin Heidenreich at the Amherst Center for Fundamental Interactions. My research bridges string theory, condensed matter physics, and computational methods.

Before coming to UMass, I received my [undergraduate degree information here]. My path to physics was shaped by a fascination with the mathematical structures underlying nature—from the geometry of extra dimensions to the entanglement patterns of quantum matter.

When not doing physics, I enjoy [hobbies/interests].

## Research Interests

- **String Theory & High-Energy Physics**
  - Geometric engineering of supersymmetric gauge theories
  - Brane tilings and orientifolds
  - Superconformal field theories and their moduli spaces

- **Condensed Matter & Many-Body Physics**
  - Boundary critical phenomena and RG flows
  - Monte Carlo algorithms for long-range interactions
  - Quantum criticality and scaling

- **Computational Methods**
  - Tensor networks (DMRG, MPS)
  - Machine learning for physics (diffusion models, flows)
  - High-performance scientific computing
